summary: Tested the Fee Type master, Fee rules (formerly EMD rules) and per-tender fees in the vendor Tender Builder, on both the backend and the UI. Backend: the new suite tests/test_r10_fee_types.py passed 33/33. Regression suites passed when run serially with -n 0: test_r9_vendor_tender_builder.py 21/21 and test_r9b_scope_fillall_dpr_sub.py 14/14. UI: the Fee types tab works (8 seeded types listed; create, edit and the delete-in-use 409 toast all work). The Fee rules tab works: the fee-type dropdown, the type summary, the single-amount layout with no range button, the 'all categories' hint, and the multi-select CategoryPicker (search, chips, count, a required tick for 'selected' types). Multi-range rules save, the list shows the fee type name and categories, and the 2 existing KZ rules open and save fine. Vendor builder: the fees panel shows 2 fees. An upfront fee that is unpaid blocks AI fill all with a 402 toast. An unpaid on-completion fee blocks submit with a 402 toast. A real Stripe test checkout (4242) returns to ?fee_session=..., shows the 'Payment received' toast, the fee shows '✓ Paid', and the transaction was marked credited. All test data has been cleaned up.

minor.issue: The upfront-fee gate can be bypassed. Section content can still be written through a full template PATCH, which sends the sections array, while an upfront fee is unpaid (verified: 200 and the body persisted, while PATCH /tender-pro/templates/{tid}/sections/{code} correctly returns 402). If 'upfront' is meant to stop all work before payment, this PATCH should keep header changes but reject section-body changes (or the bulk attachment upload) while upfront fees are unpaid. The builder's normal Save button probably uses this same PATCH, so manual typing plus Save is not blocked.
DPR analysis without a template_id skips assert_fees_paid entirely, so a vendor can still use the AI DPR analysis before paying an upfront fee. This may be acceptable by design.

success_url is /vendor/tender-builder?fee_session=... with no template id. After paying, the vendor lands on the builder with no tender open and has to find and reopen the draft to see '✓ Paid'. Suggest adding &tid= and auto-opening that tender.

issues: The 'Pct max (cap)' input still shows when the slab type is Fixed (it has no effect there)
Success toasts still say 'EMD master created/updated' instead of 'Fee rule saved'
The default slab type for a 'fixed or %' type is % even after switching from a fixed type; minor
When both an upfront and an on-completion fee are due, the submit-review 402 names the on-completion fee first. That is fine, but the panel could highlight which fee blocks which action.

action_items: Decide on and enforce the upfront gate for section content in PATCH /tender-templates/{tid}: reject section-body changes while upfront fees are unpaid, and still allow header, category and value changes
Include the template id in the fee checkout success_url and auto-open that tender after returning from Stripe
Hide 'Pct max (cap)' for Fixed slabs; rename the 'EMD master' toasts to 'Fee rule'
critical_code_review_comments: tender_builder_fees: a rule scoped to selected categories never applies until header.product_category is set. Submit requires a category, so on-completion fees are safe, but upfront fees are not charged at all while the category is empty: a vendor can work freely with no category set, then set it later.

The tender value used for fees is declared by the vendor (header.tender_value / budget_amount). Raising it later makes the difference due (verified), but nothing stops a vendor declaring a low value; the reviewer should check this.
fee_types PATCH/DELETE use ObjectId(fid) without try/except, so a malformed id gives a 500 instead of a 400/404.
Changing a fee type's code is blocked (good), but deactivating a type has no effect on rules that already exist. The type's is_active only filters tender_builder_fees.
Webhook crediting is correctly idempotent (credited flag via find_one_and_update), and the status endpoint is owner-scoped (404 for another vendor, verified).
seed_data_creation: None left behind. TEST_ fee types, rules, templates and payment_transactions were deleted; the vendor's profile ({}) and business_categories (None) were restored. The 8 seeded types and the 2 KZ rules are intact (they only received updated_at, plus categories=[] from the round-trip PATCH).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run serially: pytest tests/test_r10_fee_types.py -n 0 (it sets the vendor's KZ country and category and cleans up in teardown), then the r9 and r9b files one at a time. For the UI, log in via page.request.post to /api/v1/admin/auth/login or /api/v1/vendor/auth/login, then navigate. Open a vendor draft via [data-testid=tb-draft-{id}]. AI Fill All shows a confirm dialog, so accept dialogs. In Stripe hosted checkout: #email, #cardNumber, #cardExpiry, #cardCvc, #billingName, #billingPostalCode, uncheck #enableStripePass, then [data-testid=hosted-payment-submit-button]. Use python tests/_r10_ui_setup.py setup|cleanup for vendor fee UI data.
